How can I change a ceramic product photo to a three-quarter view while preserving its shape and material? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
Changing a 2D ceramic product photo into a three-quarter (3/4) view while preserving its shape and material characteristics requires specific tools that can manipulate depth without altering textures.
Method 1: Using Adobe Photoshop's Perspective Warp Tool
The most reliable professional method to alter an object's viewpoint non-destructively is using the Perspective Warp feature in Adobe Photoshop. Because ceramic items rely heavily on specular highlights and precise geometric curves, this tool allows you to alter the viewpoint without distorting the underlying texture or material qualities. 
YouTube
·Photoshop Training Channel
 +1
Prepare the Layer: Convert your product photo layer into a Smart Object by navigating to Filter → Convert for Smart Filters. This ensures your perspective adjustments are non-destructive and fully reversible. 
YouTube
·Photoshop Training Channel
 +2
Define the Layout: Go to Edit → Perspective Warp. You will enter Layout mode. Click and drag to create quads (grids) over the main visible faces of the ceramic item. If the item has multiple sides, snap the grids together along its edges. Match the grid corners to the existing lines of your product. 
Adobe
 +2
Warp to a Three-Quarter View: Switch to Warp mode in the options bar (or press W). Drag the anchor points to rotate the object into a three-quarter perspective. You can compress one side and extend the other to simulate depth. 
YouTube
·Photoshop Training Channel
 +2
Lock and Straighten: To keep the product standing naturally, hold the Shift key and click on vertical lines to keep them perfectly upright as you twist the grid. Press Enter to commit the changes. 
YouTube
·PS Tutelar
 +2
Method 2: Using Free Online Editors (Photopea or Mockover)
If you do not have Photoshop, advanced browser-based photo editors can replicate true projective transforms. 
YouTube
·Learn Canva with Greg
 +1
Photopea: This free platform mirrors Photoshop's mechanics. You can load your ceramic product photo, use Edit > Free Transform, right-click, and select Distort. By pulling the corner points independently, you can realistically shorten the sides of your image to form a 3D plane, maintaining the original glaze, material, and reflection details intact. 
YouTube
·Learn Canva with Greg
Mockover: This tool applies a true 3D Perspective Transform rather than a flat crop or standard skew. By dropping the image onto the canvas, you can manually adjust the four corners outward or inward using an alignment grid overlay until the graphic tilts flawlessly into a three-quarter angle. 
Mockover
 +1
Method 3: Using Generative AI Tools
For a purely hands-off approach, you can leverage AI platforms like Adobe Firefly or dedicated e-commerce photography AI suites. 
Adobe
 +1
Image-to-Image Prompts: Upload your product image into an AI background/studio generator. Use structured prompts such as: "Change the camera viewpoint of the exact product in the image to a clean three-quarter studio view, maintaining identical ceramic material texture, shape, and aspect ratio."
A platform like Adobe Firefly allows you to describe the exact perspective changes you want through its Generative Fill workspace, helping reconstruct hidden angles while attempting to stay faithful to the original item. 
Instagram
·Safwaan Mujawar
 +2

Is the ceramic product symmetrical (like a vase or bowl) or asymmetrical (like a mug with a handle)?
Do you need to reveal a completely hidden side of the product?
